info.name: Buildiq Component Blocks
info.description: Newman/Postman integration tests for the component-blocks spec (tasks.md 7.2). Covers `ComponentBlock` CRUD via the standard OR objects REST API (no bespoke controller — ADR-022) and the export/import JSON round-trip shape (design.md D4).

request.description: Saving a widget captures its config, not its data (REQ) — the created record's fragment carries structure only.

exec: // OpenRegister returns the object's identity in the `@self` envelope.
// This block asserted `to.have.property('uuid')` and then stashed
// `body.uuid` — which is undefined. Postman interpolates an undefined
// collection variable as the literal string 'null', so the next three
// requests went to `/component-block/null` and got 404. FIVE assertions
// failed, four of them in requests that had nothing wrong with them.
// A missing identifier must fail HERE, where the cause is, rather than
// as a 404 on a URL three requests later — so the accessor is tolerant
// of which field carries it and the assertion below is strict about the
pm.test('Response carries a uuid + the submitted slug', function () {
pm.expect(blockUuid, 'the create response must carry an identifier at @self.id (or uuid/id)').to.be.a('string').and.not.empty;
pm.expect(blockUuid, 'the identifier must not be the string "null" — that is an undefined variable interpolated').to.not.eql('null');

request.description: Exported block imports into a different organisation (REQ) — the import payload is the export envelope's `block` field (uuid/createdBy stripped, per blockExport.js#parseBlockImport) re-posted as a fresh record.

exec: // ⚠️ THIS ASSERTION USED TO PASS OVER TWO BROKEN VALUES.
// It read `body.uuid` (undefined, because OR puts the identifier at
// `@self.id`) and compared it to `block_uuid` (the literal string
// 'null', because the create step stashed an undefined the same way).
// `undefined !== 'null'` is true, so 'gets a NEW uuid' reported GREEN
// while neither side was a uuid at all — and the DELETE that followed
// Now both sides must actually BE identifiers before they are compared.
pm.test('imported record gets a NEW uuid, distinct from the source block', function () {
pm.expect(importedUuid, 'the imported record must carry an identifier').to.be.a('string').and.not.empty;
pm.expect(importedUuid, 'not the string "null" — that is an undefined variable interpolated').to.not.eql('null');
pm.expect(sourceUuid, 'the source block identifier must have been captured').to.be.a('string').and.not.empty;
